body:
(Adapted from MWG Exercise 3.I.2.) A consumer has wealth w>0 and initially faces prices p0. A per-unit tax t on good 1 lifts that good’s price to p10​+t; call the new price vector p1. The tax collects T=tx1​(p1,w). Write u0=v(p0,w) and u1=v(p1,w), let h1​(p1​,u) denote Hicksian demand for good 1 with the other prices held fixed, and let pˉ​1​=p10​+t be the after-tax price. MWG measure the deadweight loss in two ways, (3.I.5)

​e(p1,u1)−e(p0,u1)−T=∫p10​pˉ​1​​[h1​(p1​,u1)−h1​(pˉ​1​,u1)]dp1​​

and (3.I.6)

​e(p1,u0)−e(p0,u0)−th1​(p1,u0)=∫p10​pˉ​1​​[h1​(p1​,u0)−h1​(pˉ​1​,u0)]dp1​.​

Find the derivative of each measure with respect to t. Prove that both derivatives vanish at t=0, and that when h1​(p,u0) is strictly decreasing in p1​ both are strictly positive for every t>0.

Answer

As printed, this does not hold in full generality: the positive sign fails for L5​. Counterexample: with two goods, u=x1​x2​/(x1​+x2​), p0=(1,1), w=1 and t=24, where u0=1/4, h1​ is strictly decreasing, yet L5​ has derivative −1/3375 at t=24. The corrected statements keep both sign claims for L6​, adding that h1​ has a negative derivative at p10​+t, and the claim at t=0 for L5​, adding local nonsatiation.
